title: Rejecting a stale write
questions: Explain expected version 7 vs stored version 8, then the matching version 7 vs 7. Show the stored value stays unchanged on rejection. The comparison and write are one database statement, not two operations.

slide.title: One atomic UPDATE rejects stale writes
slide.narrative: The client supplies the version it read. The database checks the document ID and version in the same statement that writes the change. This prevents a separate check from becoming stale before the write. The function returns the result without an automatic retry.

fileSummaries.summary: Replaces unconditional writes with an atomic version check and returns 409 when no row changes.

inlineExplanations.text: Zero affected rows can mean a version mismatch or no matching document ID. Both return 409.

svgIllustration.title: Version mismatch and version match
svgIllustration.takeaway: A mismatch preserves the stored body and version. A match replaces the body and increases the version by one.
svgIllustration.assumptions: Both examples use a matching document ID. Body values Old and New are illustrative. Spacing does not represent time.

plan.question: What changes when expected version 7 differs from, or matches, the stored version?
plan.visualApproach: Show two independent rows with stored values before and after the statement. Put each comparison and its write action inside one shared atomic UPDATE boundary.
plan.whyThisForm: Aligned before and after values make the unchanged rejection state visible. The central boundary keeps the comparison and write together.
plan.encodings: Rows represent independent examples. Columns show stored state before, the atomic statement, and stored state after. Arrows connect each example to its result. Status labels sit outside the statement boundary.

scenarios.title: Reject or write
scenarios.input: Client supplies expectedVersion = 7 and body = New.

frames.title: Only a matching version permits the write
frames.caption: Read each row independently. The upper row returns 409 without a change. The lower row writes New, sets version 8, and returns 200.
